question: R buys two cars at the same price. He sells one car at a profit of 12% and the other car at a loss of 8%. Find the total percentage of his profit or loss.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the Cost Price (CP) of two articles is the same, the net profit or loss percentage is the average of their individual profit or loss percentages.

Net Profit or Loss % = (P₁ + P₂) ÷ 2

⇒ Net % = (+12% − 8%) ÷ 2

⇒ Net % = +4% ÷ 2 = +2%

Since the sign is positive, there is an overall profit of 2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 2% Profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit on the 1st car = 12%

Loss on the 2nd car = 8%

Cost Price (CP) of both cars is the same.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the CP of each car be 100.

⇒ Total CP of both cars = 100 + 100 = 200

⇒ SP of the 1st car (at 12% profit) = 100 + 12 = 112

⇒ SP of the 2nd car (at 8% loss) = 100 − 8 = 92

⇒ Total SP of both cars = 112 + 92 = 204
